prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Wildmere; priority safety>protection>export. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss, shutdown on confirmed fire; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor (condition/degradation data)→Turbine Sensor Bus. Mode Turbine Lockout: no remote restart during fire investigation. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment; mode Substation Degraded; alarms not cleared merely because detector normal. Substation Operator switches only in active window with Control Engineer authorization, notifies Grid Dispatcher. Outages: Marine Coordinator vessel timing; Electrical Technician post-isolation inspection; Work Permit Portal updated first; Duty Planner records times. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry/alarms→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); availability records; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room keeps last validated limit on comms loss. Operations Radio Console: voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft; Vessel Master read-back; Transfer Manifest Addendum from Duty Planner. Evacuation: Personnel Tracking Console; HSE Officer advises re-entry; Field Supervisor status→Shore Control Room. North/South Access Scanners: credential+area/time authorization else deny, barrier closed, no override; south anti-tailgating; denial→Field Supervisor/HSE Officer; tamper-protected log; faulty→out of service, named approver; credential-free emergency egress. East/West Service Lifts: Field Supervisor pre-shift inspection; interlocks never bypassed; load≤rated; safety defect blocks release; stop at nearest safe landing on anomaly; Personnel Tracking Console logs entry/exit. Performance: measures defined (source, method, interval, owner), change-controlled; Fleet Dispatch Console fleet status; Maintenance Planning Engine work completion; Control Engineer records deviation findings; corrective actions need owner, due date, verification; Duty Planner adjusts priorities;

New part:
S935: The system records the affected function, the detected condition, and the time of transition so that operators can assess the scope and duration of the impairment.
S936: Safety functions take priority over energy production, maintenance throughput, and schedule recovery in every degraded mode.
S937: Turbine Controller retains protective control locally when the supervisory connection is unavailable, while the Shore Control Room monitors the loss of visibility.
S938: If remote commands cannot be confirmed, the Control Engineer suspends those commands and uses approved local procedures until reliable control is restored.
S939: The Weather Service and Weather Analyst support entry into Weather Hold when forecast or observed conditions exceed approved operating limits.
S940: A turbine with a safety-critical fault is placed in Turbine Lockout until the fault is assessed and the required work is authorized.
S941: The Offshore Substation enters Substation Degraded when a protection, auxiliary supply, or monitoring impairment limits safe switching or export capability.
S942: The Grid Interface Relay applies the configured response to a Grid Constraint, and the Grid Dispatcher is advised when generation capability changes.
S943: Marine activity is reduced or suspended in Vessel Standby when weather, visibility, communications, or vessel capability is insufficient for safe transfer.
S944: The Marine Coordinator and Vessel Master confirm that personnel and vessels can remain safely accounted for during an extended interruption.
S945: The Fire Detection Panel and Emergency Generator remain essential services during degraded operation and are not bypassed to recover production.
S946: The SCADA Gateway preserves available status and alarm information, while the SCADA Engineer investigates missing or inconsistent indications.
S947: The Fleet Dispatch Console presents operational restrictions so that the Duty Planner can prioritize urgent safety work and maintainable generation capacity.
S948: The Maintenance Planning Engine separates safety-critical work from tasks that can safely wait until normal access and support are available.
S949: The HSE Officer reviews any proposed workaround that changes established access, isolation, or personnel-control arrangements.
S950: A degraded condition is escalated when its duration, uncertainty, or effect on adjacent equipment increases beyond the approved operating envelope.
S951: The Control Engineer coordinates technical recovery with the relevant field and shore roles before any protection or operating restriction is removed.
S952: Recovery begins only after the initiating condition has been corrected or bounded and the responsible operator has confirmed that the equipment is stable.
S953: Required inspections and functional checks are completed before affected equipment is returned to automatic control or normal duty.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
